quiz.title: Module 1 — Tuesday — Becoming a Clear Communicator
quiz.description: Tuesday's quiz covers the four lessons on clarity, conciseness, simplicity and precision — coherence practice, the CLEAR framework for explaining complex ideas, and why a larger usable vocabulary matters.

questions.prompt: According to the clarity lesson, what is the main skill being developed when you practise speaking coherently?
options: Memorising large amounts of information
Strengthening the connection between your thoughts and your spoken words
Speaking as quickly as possible
Using sophisticated vocabulary in every conversation
questions.explanation: Coherence practice trains the link between thought and speech — turning what is in your mind into words that come out in a clear order.

questions.prompt: In the coherence exercise, what is the purpose of using a random word generator?
options: To test how many words you know
To give you prepared topics for memorisation
To force you to organise and express your thoughts on an unexpected topic
To help you avoid speaking about unfamiliar subjects
questions.explanation: The randomness removes preparation. You have to organise your thinking on the spot, which is exactly the skill being built.

questions.prompt: How long does the video recommend speaking about the randomly generated word during the exercise?
options: 10–20 seconds
30 seconds
1–3 minutes
5–10 minutes
questions.explanation: A minute or three is long enough to force real structure, but short enough to repeat often.

questions.prompt: What is one major problem that concise communication is designed to reduce?
options: Having too much knowledge about a subject
Using unnecessary words and information that weaken the message
Speaking to people who already understand the topic
Using pauses while communicating
questions.explanation: Extra words do not add meaning — they dilute it. Conciseness removes what does not help the listener understand.

questions.prompt: When explaining a complicated idea to someone who is not familiar with the subject, what does the CLEAR framework recommend doing first?
options: Use technical language to establish credibility
Give every available detail about the subject
Calibrate the explanation to the audience's existing knowledge
Ask the listener to research the topic beforehand
questions.explanation: Start by gauging what your listener already knows. The same idea has to be pitched differently to a beginner and an expert.

questions.prompt: In the CLEAR framework, what does the “L” stand for?
options: Listen
Link
Language
Lead
questions.explanation: The L is Link — connecting the new idea to something the listener already understands.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of using analogies or metaphors when explaining a complex idea?
options: To make the explanation sound more sophisticated
To replace the need to understand the subject
To connect an unfamiliar idea to something the listener already understands
To make the explanation longer and more detailed
questions.explanation: An analogy gives the listener something familiar to hang the new idea on, which is what makes it land.

questions.prompt: According to the lesson on articulation and word choice, why is having a larger usable vocabulary valuable to a communicator?
options: It allows the speaker to use complicated words in every situation.
It makes the speaker appear more intelligent than the listener.
It gives the speaker more language options for expressing thoughts precisely.
It eliminates the need to organise thoughts before speaking.
questions.explanation: A larger usable vocabulary means more options when you reach for the right word — which is precision, not complexity.
